episodes.194719: Ahead of a closed low pressure system scattered thunderstorms developed from Lemhi County into Southwest Montana. Storms produced brief heavy rain and strong outflow winds.
episodes.194720: Ahead of a closed low pressure system scattered thunderstorms developed from Lemhi County into Southwest Montana. Storms produced brief heavy rain and strong outflow winds.
episodes.195314: Scattered convection developed in advance of an approaching shortwave trough digging through the Pacific Northwest. This convection resulted in some isolated instances of severe wind gusts.
episodes.195834: A waterspout was reported off of Stuart Beach.
episodes.195879: An upper level trough passed across the Northern Rockies September 11, which allowed for numerous thunderstorms to develop in the afternoon. Thermodynamic and kinematic ingredients were sufficient for a few strong thunderstorms, mostly across Southwest Montana. Additionally, a series of thunderstorms moved across the Horse Gulch burn scar, which resulted in flash flooding.
episodes.196264: A stalled front across central FL and strong high pressure over the mid-Atlantic region continued strong onshore flow across the local area. Above normal moisture and passing short wave trough energy from the west to southwest continued to fuel localized heavy flooding rainfall. In addition to the heavy rainfall, gusty winds of 35-45 mph were starting to cause isolated trees to blown on due to saturated grounds, including in Duval county.
episodes.196467: An area of upper low pressure to the north of Nevada created conditions to produce some isolated thunderstorms along with some strong wind gusts across northern Nevada over a two day period as the cold front moved east into Montana.
episodes.196579: A line of instability stretching over Lower Idaho Panhandle generated thunderstorms and heavy rain during the afternoon of September 11 2024. The storms caused a debris flow near the Gwen Fire burn scar and generated a funnel cloud over Mann Lake near Lapwai.

events.narrative: The CAMEL BACK MTN mesonet station recorded a wind gust of 62 mph as a result of outflow winds associated with a nearby cluster of showers and thunderstorms moving through the area.

The WHITE SAGE mesonet station recorded an initial peak wind gust of 71 mph, followed by an additional gust of 63 mph, as a result of outflow winds associated with a nearby cluster of showers and thunderstorms moving through the area.
The DUGWAY-S mesonet station recorded a wind gust of 60 mph as a result of outflow winds associated with a nearby cluster of showers and thunderstorms moving through the area.
The CENEWS mesonet station recorded a wind gust of 62 mph as a result of outflow winds associated with a nearby cluster of showers and thunderstorms moving through the area.
A member of the public reported seeing a waterspout over the Atlantic Ocean off of Stuart Beach. It remained over the water.

At 11:45 am, law enforcement reported a vehicle was stuck due to street flooding in the intersection of Gran Bay Parkway and Corklan Drive. At 1:26 pm, law enforcement reported several vehicles were stuck in flood water at Gran Bay Parkway and Old St. Augustine Road.

Public report via social media stated rocks on Highway 12 within the Gwen Fire burn scar. This was confirmed by dispatch. Rocks were cleared and highway remained open. Nearby gauges reported 0.40 of an inch to 0.80 of an inch of rain over the last 18 hours.
Thunderstorm outflow winds were observed, with a radar estimated time of 2:47 pm MDT. Minor structural damage to the Incident Command Post for the Johnson Fire but no injuries.
Ten inches to one foot of standing flood water cover the roads near the intersection of Marathon Parkway and Timuquana Road. There were no stranded vehicles.
Thunderstorm outflow wind gusts. No damage noted in Butte.
Public reported to local media an EF0 funnel cloud near Mann Lake at 1613 PDT. No damage reported.
Thunderstorm outflow wind gusts, no damage noted. Mesocyclone/wall cloud observed from MacDonald Pass webcam with this thunderstorm.
Strong cold front triggered thunderstorms and caused the temperature to drop from 59 degrees to 46 in an hour. Wind gust occurred with thunderstorm outflow. No storm damage noted.
Ambient Weather Sensor near East Helena measured a severe gust.
